Article Title: ‘There is no accountability’: Sonam Wangchuk seeks answers on Leh violence inquiry
Article Text:
Sonam Wangchuk questions inquiry into Leh violence

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk on Sunday questioned the status of the inquiry into the violence in Leh, saying a year had passed since the incidents and that those responsible were yet to be held accountable. He also raised concerns over the pending legal cases and the compensation for those who were killed.Wangchuk said he had travelled to Delhi to draw attention to the unresolved issues surrounding the violence and his subsequent imprisonment in Jodhpur."I had to come to Delhi to inform the country that a year has passed since those incidents in Ladakh, incidents that led to my own imprisonment in Jodhpur. I want to ask: what became of the findings of the inquiry commission set up regarding those incidents? When will the officials, the Governor, the Lieutenant Governor, and the Home Minister, who ordered such actions, provide answers? The issue remains unresolved. Those who were martyred have not yet received appropriate and dignified compensation. Legal cases are still pending against people, and many are left in a wretched state. There is no accountability."Protests demanding statehood for Ladakh and safeguards under the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution turned violent on September 24, 2025, leaving four people dead and several others injured. The Union Territory administration subsequently ordered a judicial inquiry into the incident.Wangchuk was detained under the National Security Act (NSA) two days after the violence and was released in March this year.On the Election Commission of India row, Wangchuk said he supported organisations and leaders raising concerns over the electoral process and accountability, while acknowledging that he could not personally participate in every movement."I always extend my moral support to all organizations and leaders raising such issues, issues that are entirely valid, such as cleaning up the election process and ensuring accountability. However, it is not possible for me to personally join every single movement. I hope the entire country will join in demanding this accountability to build a clean, transparent democracy."The remarks come amid a political row over reported objections by two Election Commissioners to decisions related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Opposition parties have demanded action against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, a halt to the SIR exercise and fresh elections in states where polls have already been held.The BJP, however, has defended the Election Commission, with party spokesperson Sambit Patra saying that dissent within the poll panel was a sign of a “vibrant democracy”.
Article Summary: Sonam Wangchuk questions the status of the inquiry into the violence in Leh. He also raised concerns over the pending legal cases and the compensation for those who were killed. Protests demanding statehood for Ladakh turned violent on September 24, 2025, leaving four people dead.

Article Title: As Trump hugs Xi and plugs Sharif, India feels the squeeze
Article Text:
Trump’s outreach to Xi and praise for Sharif come as India faces a more transactional US relationship

TOI correspondent from Washington:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The clearest sign yet of a widening US-India diplomatic rift came this weekend from the White House and the United Nations, where India was denouncing Pakistan for what it called a litany of “falsehoods” and “deceit,” even as US President Donald Trump appeared to give those very claims a presidential imprimatur.Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had used his UN General Assembly address to revive Islamabad’s account of the 2025 India-Pakistan conflict, crediting Trump with a “timely intervention” that, he said, prevented a wider war. On Friday night, shortly after China’s President Xi Jinping had departed for Beijing, Trump posted an 87-second excerpt of Sharif’s speech on Truth Social without comment. The clip included Sharif’s praise of Trump and Pakistan Army chief Asim Munir.The timing was striking. India had just exercised its Right of Reply, with First Secretary Petal Gahlot accusing Islamabad of peddling “falsehoods” and “deceit” and describing Pakistan as a “puppet” regime. New Delhi has also rejected Trump’s repeated assertion that he mediated the cessation of hostilities in May 2025, saying the fighting was halted after direct military-to-military communication between India and Pakistan.For India, however, the larger concern may be less about one Truth Social post than about a pattern. The Xi visit to Washington this week appeared to underscore how dramatically the strategic geometry of US foreign policy has shifted. Rather than organizing its Asia policy principally around building India as a counterweight to China – a two-decade old Washington objective that resulting in an “Indo-Pacific” focused QUAD – the Trump White House increasingly appears willing to deal with Beijing as a peer whose cooperation is indispensable, and whose confrontation carries costs Trump is reluctant to incur.Following the Xi visit, Washington and Beijing extended their trade truce and agreed on tariff reductions covering $30 billion of less-sensitive goods in each direction, according reports in the Chinese media. They also operationalized bilateral boards on trade and investment and agreed to pursue an artificial-intelligence dialogue.Analysts say none of this amounts to a formal US-China condominium, and deep disagreements over Taiwan, technology, trade and strategic competition remain. But the emerging arrangement has prompted comparisons with a de facto G-2: Washington and Beijing managing their rivalry directly while other powers, including India, find themselves having to adjust to decisions made in a room in which they are not present.“One totally unsurprising consequence of this US-China trade truce is that Trump is not even thinking about implementing the Lindsey Graham Russia sanctions legislation he just signed, which would have required penalizing China's support for Russia's war machine,” Tom Malinowski a former New Jersey lawmaker noted, even as Republicans close to Trump have been champing at the bit to punish New Delhi. The Graham bill, signed by Trump on Sept. 18, gives the president authority to impose tariffs of up to 100% on countries that continue buying Russian crude or natural gas under specified conditions. The law specifically covers countries among the five largest Russian oil or gas importers that make new purchases, as well as countries identified among the top facilitators of sanctions evasion.India is plainly exposed to that provision, as is China. Yet the contrast in Trump’s handling of the two relationships has become difficult for New Delhi to ignore: Beijing is being courted into a new economic accommodation even as India faces the prospect of punitive trade action.The message was reinforced this week by a senior State Department official who said the Graham law gives Trump “a new tool in his toolbox,” while emphasizing that its use is not automatic. The official pointed to a broad national-security waiver but added that Washington expects India to help the US end the Ukraine war.More revealing was the official's description of what Washington now wants from India: not necessarily strategic alignment against China, but access to the enormous Indian energy market. “We are looking to also become a huge source of India's energy needs,” the official was quoted as saying, pointing to expanding US hydrocarbon exports and urging faster diversification away from Russian supplies.All this is consequential because for two decades the bipartisan American strategy had been to help India acquire the economic, military and technological heft to balance China's rise. As recently as May, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who will be back in New Delhi in October, was describing India as one of America's most important strategic partners, while US officials continued to characterize New Delhi as a critical Indo-Pacific counterweight.The language now coming from Washington is noticeably more transactional.For New Delhi, the resulting unease is not simply about tariffs or Pakistan. It is about whether a strategic partnership painstakingly built across successive administrations is being replaced by a transactional relationship in which China is too powerful to punish, Pakistan is useful to cultivate, and India is expected to accommodate. And as New Delhi watched Washington kiss up to Beijing as an indispensable peer and embrace a country New Delhi views as a terrorism sponsor, the strategic space India once occupied in the American imagination appeared to be shrinking.
Article Summary: Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had used his UN General Assembly address to revive Islamabad’s account of the 2025 India-Pakistan conflict. On Friday night, shortly after Xi Jinping had departed for Beijing, Trump posted an 87-second excerpt of Sharif's speech on Truth Social without comment. India had just exercised its Right of Reply, with First Secretary Petal Gahlot accusing Islamabad of peddling “falsehoods” and “deceit”

Article Title: 2 more Naga men killed as ethnic violence flares up in Manipur again
Article Text:
Manipur violence claims another life as gunmen strike Senapati village

Two Mao Naga men were shot dead by unidentified gunmen at Kalenjang village in Manipur's Senapati district Saturday afternoon, with two others wounded, in the latest escalation in a Naga-Kuki conflict that has claimed more than 40 lives since Feb.The shooting took place under Senapati police station around 2.30pm, shortly after CM Yumnam Khemchand Singh left a function about 30km away. It came two days after four Tangkhul Naga men were killed allegedly by Myanmar-based Kuki National Army-Burma (B) at Pilong village near the international border in Kamjong district.The Kalenjang and Pilong killings are part of a series of Naga-Kuki clashes that began in Feb, shortly after Singh's govt took charge. At least 21 people - 11 Nagas and 10 Kukis, including a pregnant woman - have been killed since Aug 27. The toll is separate from the Meitei-Kuki conflict, which has killed over 300.Both the communities have accused militant groups from the other side of the attacks. Police have said several such allegations are under investigation and have not been independently verified.The killings came as United Naga Council (UNC), the apex body of Naga tribes in Manipur, called off its 131-day economic blockade of NH-2 and NH-37 after a meeting with home ministry and Manipur govt at the BSF Frontier headquarters in Guwahati Saturday.The blockade followed the abduction of six Liangmai Naga civilians in Kangpokpi district.Manipur Congress president Okram Ibobi Singh accused BJP-headed NDA govts in the state and Centre of remaining "silent spectators" to civilian killings. "Govt is behaving as if it is not concerned about the killings of civilians of any community," the former three-time CM said. "We strongly condemn the killings of innocent civilians from Naga, Kuki and Meitei communities," he said, while questioning security along the Myanmar border.
Article Summary: Two Mao Naga men shot dead by unidentified gunmen at Kalenjang village in Manipur's Senapati district. Two others wounded, in the latest escalation in a Naga-Kuki conflict that has claimed more than 40 lives since Feb.

Students at Lovely Professional University (LPU) in Punjab’s Phagwara damaged property and blocked the Jalandhar-Phagwara national highway early Sunday following unverified reports on social media about the alleged rape of a female student. Police said they had no information of any such crime.Kapurthala Senior Superintendent of Police Gaurav Toora said police received information around 1.45 am that students had gathered on the LPU campus and blocked a road. Addressing the unverified rape claim, Toora said, "When we reached here, we came to know that there were rumours. Because of the rumours, students gathered here".Videos circulating on social media showed students damaging window panes and flower pots, while some objects were also seen being set on fire. The students also blocked the Jalandhar-Phagwara national highway.Toora said police spoke to students who raised issues with the LPU administration and that efforts were being made to address their concerns."We spoke to students who had some issues with the LPU administration.We heard them and are trying to get them resolved. The situation is completely under control," the SSP said.He added that students told police their grievances were not being addressed properly. An assessment of the property damage is under way, and necessary legal action will be taken, Toora said.A heavy police force has been deployed at the university, with police stating that the situation is now under control.The incident came a day after students at Chitkara University in Patiala held a protest following unverified claims on social media that two female students had allegedly died by suicide on the campus. Students had also damaged a police vehicle during that protest.
Article Summary: Students at Lovely Professional University (LPU) damaged property and blocked the Jalandhar-Phagwara national highway early Sunday. Police say rumours triggered campus unrest following unverified reports on social media about the alleged rape of a female student. Police said they had no information of any such crime.

Article Title: ‘Congress part of every conspiracy’: CM Yogi hits out at opposition amid 'dissent within EC' row

NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath defended the Election Commission amid the "dissent within the poll body" row, while slamming the Congress party for "creating confusion and targeting constitutional institutions".Tearing into the rival Congress for criticisng the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, the Uttar Pradesh CM said: "The current SIR exercise was not the first such revision undertaken by the Election Commission, pointing to similar exercises conducted in 1952, 1957, 1961, 1965–66 and 2003.""Regarding the SIR (Special Intensive Revision), the confusion that has been consistently created by them (opposition parties), it is not as if the current Election Commission is the first to undertake such an exercise; in the past—often under Congress-led governments—similar exercises were conducted in 1952, 1957, 1961, 1965–66, and even in 2003. Despite this history, the uproar raised by the Congress, Samajwadi Party, RJD, and other parties over the current SIR exercise is extremely unfortunate. "He said the Election Commission had already clarified that eligible voters who were left out would be given an opportunity to submit the required form. He also referred to the Supreme Court’s position on the Election Commission’s action regarding Form 6."All three Election Commissioners came before the press and clarified the situation.Regarding SIR, directions had already been issued that all eligible voters who were left out would be given an opportunity to fill the form. The Supreme Court has also upheld the Election Commission's action regarding Form 6. Despite this, putting the Election Commission and Chief Election Commissioners in the dock, questioning every constitutional institution and attempting to tarnish India's image globally is extremely unfortunate. Congress and its allies should control their irresponsible actions. There should be no place for violence, vandalism or misinformation in a democracy."Adityanath further accused the Congress and other opposition parties of undermining constitutional institutions and democratic values for political interests."The approach of the Congress and opposition parties has always been to be a part of every conspiracy to harm the constitutional institutions of India and weaken the democratic values ​​for their political interests, due to which the world's largest democracy can be harmed. It is surprising that the current actions and rhetoric of the country's main opposition party and other parties associated with the UPA alliance are extremely irresponsible and damaging to democratic values. "Adityanath also criticised the Congress over its objections to EVMs, noting that Congress governments had been formed at the Centre and in several states through elections conducted using the machines. He linked the criticism to what he described as a broader pattern of questioning democratic institutions."The EVMs, through which Congress governments have also been formed at the Centre and in several states, have been called a black box, raising questions about India's electoral system and the country's democratic values. Recall that on June 25, 1975, Congress sinned by undermining the Constitution by imposing the Emergency. Congress-led governments also repeatedly dismissed elected governments of opposition parties through unconstitutional means. Their actions have repeatedly compromised the country's internal and external security. Questioning the valour of the Indian armed forces during the Balakot airstrike and attempting to cast doubt on the bravery of Indian soldiers during Operation Sindoor are examples of this approach."The remarks come amid a major political confrontation over reported objections raised by two Election Commissioners to decisions related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Opposition parties have demanded action against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, an immediate halt to the SIR exercise and fresh elections in states where polls have already been held.The ruling BJP, however, defended the Election Commission, saying differences expressed by Election Commissioners during internal deliberations demonstrated that the poll panel was functioning democratically rather than under a “dictatorial” system
Article Summary: Yogi Adityanath hits out at opposition over SIR row. Uttar Pradesh chief minister slams Congress party for "creating confusion and targeting constitutional institutions" Opposition parties have demanded action against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, an immediate halt to the SIR exercise and fresh elections.

Article Title: Vijay government exempts Tamil Nadu Public (Law & Order) department from RTI- what it means
Article Text:
Tamil Nadu CM C Joseph Vijay

What the exemption means

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you support the exemption of the Public (Law and Order) Department from the RTI Act? Yes No 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: The Tamil Nadu government led by CM C Joseph Vijay has exempted the Public (Law and Order) Department from the ambit of the Right to Information (RTI) Act, classifying it as an Intelligence and Security Organisation under Section 24(4) of the law.A Gazette notification issued by the state government places the department under the exemption framework applicable to intelligence and security organisations. The move means information held by the department will generally be outside the scope of RTI requests, subject to the statutory exceptions under the Act.The Public (Law and Order) Department deals with matters concerning policing, public order and law-and-order administration and RTI Act is a law to provide for setting out the practical regime of right to information for citizens wherein they can secure access to information under the control of public authorities.This exemption could therefore affect RTI requests seeking information relating to communal incidents, political agitations, police actions and other law-and-order matters handled by the department.The statement reads, "Gazette notification dated September 21, 2026, issued by the Human Resources Management Department, the Governor, exercising powers under Section 24(4) of the Right to Information Act, 2005, has specified the Public (Law and Order) Department as an "Intelligence and Security Organization" established by the Tamil Nadu government, "for which the said Act shall not apply."However, Section 24 of the RTI Act does not provide a blanket exemption. Even organisations covered by the provision are required to provide information relating to allegations of corruption and human-rights violations, subject to the procedure prescribed under the law.Tamil Nadu has previously used the provision to exclude organisations including the Tamil Nadu State Vigilance Commission and the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu government exempts Public (Law and Order) Department from the Right to Information (RTI) Act, classifying it as an Intelligence and Security Organisation. The move means information held by the department will generally be outside the scope of RTI requests, subject to the statutory exceptions under the Act.

Article Title: BJP allies close ranks, flay opposition for 'undermining democracy'
Article Text:
Andhra Pradesh CM N Chandrababu Naidu backed the Election Commission’s statement on SIR, saying it reaffirmed the integrity and credibility of constitutional institutions

NEW DELHI: BJP's allies on Saturday closed ranks to hit out at opposition, with TDP chief and Andhra Pradesh CM N Chandrababu Naidu saying EC's statement reaffirmed "the integrity and credibility of our constitutional institutions" and ended "misconceptions" around it. "Attempts to undermine global confidence in India's democratic framework for short-term political gains are deeply unfortunate," he said, urging opposition to accept wins and losses with grace.LJP (Ram Vilas)'s Chirag Paswan said opposition is spreading confusion and questioned why it keeps silent on states where it has formed govt.JDU member Sanjay Jha said rising frustration over poll defeats have led opposition to spread propaganda to undermine the democracy.Shiv Sena's Eknath Shinde said Congress keeps mum when it wins but attacks EC when it loses. The united stand came a day after some allies had pressed EC to clarify concerns raised in media reports.

Article Title: Bangladeshi woman says Bengaluru hospital withheld husband’s body for 8 days over Rs 35L bill; High Commission intervenes
Article Text:
Tangila Islam Asha with her husband, Mohd Abdul Hakim Shabuj, when he was alive. (PC: Tangila Islam Asha)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A 26-year-old Bangladeshi woman has alleged that a leading private hospital in Bengaluru withheld her husband’s body for eight days over unpaid dues of Rs 35.79 lakh and retained her passport after he died during treatment. She received the body on Saturday after seeking help from Bangladesh High Commission. The hospital confirmed releasing the body but did not respond to her allegations. The hospital later said the patient had undergone critical care and surgical treatment after arriving with severe breathing difficulty and died despite the efforts of its medical teams.Tangila Islam Asha, 26, of Naugaon, told TOI that she and her husband, Mohammed Abdul Hakim Shabuj, 32, a contractual govt teacher in Bangladesh, arrived in Bengaluru on Sept 5 for treatment of his kidney ailment. Shabuj was admitted to ICU at Manipal Hospital on Old Airport Road the next day after developing severe chest pain and breathing difficulty.Asha said Shabuj underwent multiple procedures over the following days and his right leg was amputated on Sept 14 after it developed an infection. His condition subsequently deteriorated and he died around 1.30pm on Sept 18.“During his treatment, I paid a total of Rs 7.5 lakh in several instalments whenever they asked.After his death, I was trying to understand how I would take his body back to Bangladesh when the hospital asked me to pay Rs 35.79 lakh and said the body would not be released without payment,” Asha told TOI.She alleged that the hospital neither provided receipts for the Rs 7.5 lakh nor gave her a prior cost estimate or explanation for the outstanding amount. “I was completely helpless. After they withheld the body for eight days and retained my passport, I wrote to hospital management and also contacted Bangladesh High Commission for help. Finally, they handed over the body on Saturday after making the dues nil,” she said.Mohammed Moqtadir Hossain, Shabuj’s friend from West Bengal, who travelled to Bengaluru after learning of her situation, said local activists helped Asha recover her passport on Friday and complete formalities for taking the body home. “Apart from the Rs 7.5 lakh she had already paid, she paid nothing more,” he told TOI.When contacted, a Manipal Hospital office-bearer confirmed that the body was handed over on Saturday but declined to respond to Asha’s allegations. In a statement issued later, the hospital said Shabuj arrived with severe breathing difficulty, was found hypoxic and shifted to ICU, where he suffered a cardiac arrest and was resuscitated twice before being put on ECMO and ventilator support.The hospital said surgeons performed a pulmonary thromboendarterectomy on Sept 9 after tests showed clot formation and blockages in several regions. “Despite best efforts from the critical care as well as the surgical team, the patient succumbed to his illnesses on 18th September 2026,” it said.’
Article Summary: Tangila Islam Asha, 26, received the body on Saturday after seeking help from Bangladesh High Commission. Manipal Hospital confirmed releasing the body but did not respond to her allegations. The hospital said the patient had undergone critical care and surgical treatment after arriving with severe breathing difficulty and died despite the efforts of its medical teams.

Article Title: ‘Damage control’ after EC row: Congress demands SIR rollback, CEC’s resignation
Article Text:
Congress leader Jairam Ramesh said the Commission had issued the statement only after the media reports and nationwide protests seeking Kumar's removal.

Congress questions EC's explanation

Congress raises questions over voter deletions

Dispute over Gen Z voters

NEW DELHI: The Congress on Saturday demanded the immediate suspension of the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and called for chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation or prosecution. Their demand comes after the Election Commission issued a fresh statement defending its decisions amid reported differences within the poll body.Congress leaders Pawan Khera and Jairam Ramesh accused the EC of going into "damage control" mode following an Indian Express report and subsequent media coverage on differences between the three election commissioners. The party alleged that the SIR exercise had led to the "disenfranchisement" of crores of voters and questioned the Commission's explanation on changes to Form 6, used to add names to electoral rolls."The ECI's press note today is too lame, too little, too late," Congress' head of media and publicity department Pawan Khera said.Ramesh said the Commission had issued the statement only after the media reports and nationwide protests seeking Kumar's removal."It has just issued a wishy-washy Press Note that raises further questions on its intent, integrity, impartiality and credibility," he said on X."The ongoing SIR, which has turned out to be a method of massive disenfranchisement of several crores of Indians, must be suspended immediately without delay."In the meantime, nothing short of the CEC's resignation or prosecution will suffice," he said in a two-page statement.The Election Commission said all SIR orders were issued after approval from all three Election Commissioners. It also said changes to Form 6 had been upheld by the Supreme Court.The Commission further said letters written by Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi to the Cabinet Secretary were not related to any policy decision of the Commission or its IT division. According to the EC, the letters concerned the functioning of an officer deputed to the poll body.Ramesh said the EC statement did not directly deny the findings reported by the Indian Express."First, the Press note does not directly deny the story or its findings. It makes a defensive attempt to downplay the same in paragraph 3(i) and 3(ii) but does not say that the allegations are baseless," he said.On Goa, he said the EC's response showed that 81 of the 97 deleted voters had already filled Form 6 to be included again in the electoral rolls."To put this another way, you disenfranchise voters through a broken and corrupt system, and when caught say that they are being added back," Ramesh said.Khera also alleged that the EC had not addressed objections raised by the other two Election Commissioners over changes to Form 6."That objection was not resolved then. It was not resolved since. And this 'mother of all objections' has still not been addressed - even after today's so-called unanimous meeting," Khera said on X."So until the ECI answers this specific legal objection, no length of press notes, no claim of unanimity or any other clownery can save Gyanesh Kumar Gupta's face," he said."It is still not too late for him. He should resign and turn approver, or prepare for jail," Khera added.Ramesh also questioned the EC's reliance on a Supreme Court order of May 27 saying the order had preceded the recent media revelations."The order which was pronounced well before the recent revelations will not save the CEC for the malicious deletion of targeted voters, for the incompetence that has resulted in citizens being wiped off the roles, for the crores lost in both expenses and man-hours due to the confusion and harassment caused to entire families," he said.He also questioned the extension of voter registration deadlines in Delhi and Maharashtra and asked what would happen to voters in Karnataka, Telangana, Bihar and West Bengal."What happens to the voters disenfranchised in Bihar and West Bengal? Do the voters of these and other states who were deleted due to one man's corruption not deserve answers," Ramesh said.The Congress leader also criticised the EC's decision to involve experts from IITs and IIITs to review the ECINET portal and submit a report on whether it complies with rules."Aside from being a meaningless safeguard (since the concern is not about the technical soundness but rather the centralization which prevents voter addition at ground level) this confirms the concerns attributed to the two other Election Commissioners per the reportage," he said.Ramesh alleged that the EC's statement had not addressed concerns over the deletion of young voters."The Press Note avoids answering the questions regarding the deliberate targeting of Gen Z voters. The ECI has no answer for its targeted disenfranchisement, beginning mid-July through wholly illegal changes made to Form 6 (unseen and unapproved by Parliament) which placed an unfair burden on them to find and disclose their parents and/or grandparents' details," he said.He listed several allegations that he said required answers, including the "unilateral nature of decision making by the CEC", alleged bias against the Opposition, alleged participation in "vote chori", the enrolment of Gen Z voters and alleged negligence in the deletion and updating of electoral rolls.Ramesh said the CEC could not avoid scrutiny through bureaucratic procedures."He stands exposed and is now petrified as an entire country seeks to hold him accountable," Ramesh said.
Article Summary: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh said the Commission had issued the statement only after the media reports and nationwide protests seeking Kumar's removal. The party alleged that the SIR exercise had led to the "disenfranchisement" of crores of voters and questioned the Commission's explanation on changes to Form 6.

Article Title: 'Not talking on behalf of EC': Union minister says 'no proof' of EC-SIR row, slams opposition
Article Text:
Election officials during a meeting amid the ongoing SIR controversy

NEW DELHI: Union minister Prahlad Joshi on Saturday hit out at the opposition over its protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar amid the ongoing controversy surrounding the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, saying there was no “concrete proof” to support the allegations being raised against the Election Commission.Reacting to the opposition's claims, Joshi said the protest was an expression of the “pain” caused by its electoral defeat. He said the SIR issue was being used to voice that distress.“The pain in their hearts caused by their defeat... they are trying to express that distress through the SIR issue,” Joshi said.His remarks came in response to questions about a report published by The Indian Express, which cited concerns allegedly raised within the Election Commission over the SIR exercise. The report claimed that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised 14 written dissents or objections over a 10-month period.The reports led the opposition to seek action against CEC Gyanesh Kumar and demand a halt to the SIR, while the ECI said internal notes, queries and differences of view are part of its functioning and maintained that all final decisions on the exercise were unanimous.Joshi said that even if the report was taken into consideration, it did not amount to conclusive evidence of wrongdoing.“Whatever has appeared in The Indian Express... if you even believe that, I am not saying they have no right, but I am also saying that it is not concrete proof for that. It is not at all concrete proof,” he said.Joshi also disputed the opposition's suggestion that decisions related to the SIR were taken unilaterally. Referring to the Election Commission's own press release, he said decisions of the poll panel had been unanimous.“And whatever has been written in The Indian Express, even that never states that a unilateral decision was taken. All the decisions—all, I am not saying almost—all the decisions of the Election Commission have been taken unanimously,” Joshi said.The Union minister, however, clarified that he was not speaking on behalf of the poll panel.“I am not talking on behalf of the Election Commission, but I am speaking based on the press release issued by the Election Commission,” Joshi said.The opposition has been protesting against CEC Gyanesh Kumar over the SIR exercise and has raised questions about the manner in which the electoral-roll revision is being conducted.
Article Summary: Union minister Prahlad Joshi hit out at the opposition over its protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. He said there was no “concrete proof” to support the allegations being raised against the Election Commission. Joshi said the protest was an expression of the “pain” caused by its electoral defeat.

Article Title: 'Committed to protecting students' right to protest': CJI Surya Kant at Patna law university event
Article Text:
CJI Surya Kant (File photo)

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Saturday asserted that the judiciary would not “look the other way” when students’ fundamental right to hold peaceful protests is "infringed."The CJI made the remarks during an “unfiltered interaction” with students at Chanakya National Law University (CNLU) in Patna. According to a university statement, he told the students that he preferred a "frank question-and-answer session. "During the interaction, a student asked the CJI about the “police response to peaceful students’ protests”.According to the statement, CJI Kant told the student that “courts will not look the other way” in cases involving alleged police brutality. He also “unequivocally reaffirmed the judiciary’s commitment to protecting students’ peaceful right to protest."The reference was to the Jantar Mantar protests in Delhi against the NEET exam paper leaks, spearheaded by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), a youth pressure group. The CJP began as a satirical online campaign following the CJI’s “cockroaches” remark in the Supreme Court, which he later clarified had been reported out of context.A CJP-called march to Parliament on July 20 ended in clashes between protesters and Delhi Police and other security forces.The protests were called off on July 25 after then-Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned, fulfilling the CJP’s principal demand. The group had also sought an assurance that no student who participated in the demonstrations would be booked.On September 1, a CJI-led bench quashed the FIRs registered in connection with the July 20 clashes after the Centre and state governments assured the Supreme Court that cases against the protesters would not be pursued and no fresh FIRs would be registered over the same incidents.The order, however, does not apply to 2,873 people with criminal backgrounds who were identified at the Jantar Mantar demonstrations.
Article Summary: The CJI made the remarks during an “unfiltered interaction” with students at Chanakya National Law University (CNLU) in Patna. The reference was to the Jantar Mantar protests in Delhi against the NEET exam paper leaks.

Article Title: 'Only those who elected us can dissolve us': J&K dy CM on BJP's demand for Omar govt dismissal
Article Text:
J&K deputy CM comments came a day after BJP MLAs, led by Sham Lal Sharma, demanded the immediate dismissal of the National Conference-led government.

BJP accuses government of overstepping constitutional domain

Deputy CM attacks BJP over assembly proceedings

Statehood restoration remains key issue

NEW DELHI: Jammu and Kashmir deputy chief minister Surinder Choudhary hit out at the BJP over its demand for the dismissal of the Omar Abdullah-led government, saying any attempt to interfere with an elected government would amount to an assault on democracy and the Constitution.Choudhary made the remarks after reviewing the progress of ongoing work at the new legislative assembly complex in Jammu. His comments came a day after BJP MLAs, led by Sham Lal Sharma, demanded the immediate dismissal of the National Conference-led government.Questioning the BJP's demand, Choudhary said the government had been elected by the people and asked what right the BJP had to seek its removal."If anyone can dissolve us, it is only those who elected us," Choudhary told reporters.He was responding to the BJP's criticism of the government after Chief Minister Omar Abdullah moved a resolution in the assembly demanding the restoration of full statehood to Jammu and Kashmir.Sharma had accused the National Conference government of attempting to revive an earlier political arrangement and challenge the constitutional framework.He alleged that the assembly resolution on statehood and related issues sought to revive matters linked to autonomy and the pre-1953 constitutional arrangement.Reacting to the demand for the government's dismissal, Choudhary said, "...this means you want to resort to hooliganism and use force and coercion. That is exactly what we have been saying -- that the BJP resorts to such tactics."He added that any attempt by the BJP to interfere with the functioning of the Jammu and Kashmir government or "block our freedom would amount to an assault on democracy and the Constitution".Choudhary also accused the BJP of being "anti-democracy, anti-constitutional and anti-public", alleging that its actions and statements were against the interests of the people."When you oppose a government elected by the people, you are going against those who voted for it," he said, adding that such conduct amounted to "treason".Choudhary also criticised the BJP's conduct during the ongoing autumn session of the Jammu and Kashmir Assembly.He said the government wanted to focus on its work, while accusing the opposition party of prioritising political confrontation."They kept saying, we will corner them. But what did they actually corner? Instead, they themselves ended up in trouble after coming to the assembly," he said.Choudhary challenged the BJP to explain what it had done during the first three days of the session for the people."If the BJP is honest, let it tell us what work it has done in the last three days of the assembly session in the interest of the people," he said, accusing the party of carrying "bundles of lies".He alleged that the BJP had attempted to corner the government on social media but had failed to do so on the floor of the House, where issues could be debated through the constitutional process.On the demand for restoration of statehood, Choudhary said the absence of statehood had weakened the ability of ordinary people to have their grievances addressed.He also accused the BJP of using police action against sections of society, including poor people, shopkeepers and journalists. He alleged that shops had been demolished and journalists who sought to publish reports critical of the government had faced pressure."If statehood is restored, I can say with confidence that these things will not continue," he said.Choudhary further alleged that journalists, employees, farmers and students were being prevented from speaking freely."If it were up to the BJP, they would impose Army rule across the entire country," he said, while alleging that the party's approach amounted to "hooliganism".
Article Summary: Jammu and Kashmir deputy chief minister Surinder Choudhary hit out at the BJP over its demand for the dismissal of the Omar Abdullah-led government. He said any attempt to interfere with an elected government would amount to an assault on democracy and the Constitution. He was responding to the BJP's criticism of the government after Chief Minister Omar Abdullah moved a resolution demanding the restoration of full statehood.

Article Title: LPU students protest, block highway, set objects on fire over unverified rape report
Article Text:
(Image Credit: X) Videos circulating on social media showed students damaging window panes, flower pots and even putting some objects on fire.





CHANDIGARH: An unverified allegation that a girl student had been raped in a hostel triggered a protest at Lovely Professional University late Saturday night, with students later going on a rampage on the campus and blocking the Jalandhar-Phagwara national highway.Videos circulating on social media showed students damaging window panes and flower pots on the university campus, while some objects were also seen being set on fire.The students also blocked the Jalandhar-Phagwara national highwayPolice officials said there was no complaint and that even during the protests, students could not provide any details about the alleged victim. LPU refuted the "false and fabricated rumours" and blamed anti-social elements for the mischief.Cops managed to persuade the students to lift the blockade in the morning, but they blocked the highway again, affecting traffic to parts of Punjab, Himachal Pradesh and Jammu & Kashmir.Kapurthala SSP Gaurav Toora said the pattern matched the trouble at Chitkara University, as here too the unrest started with hearsay about the alleged rape of a student, but nobody knew about the victim or the accused. First, it was being said that the victim had committed suicide, and then it was said that she had been made to disappear and that the warden had also been changed."A statement of the students has been recorded and we are investigating. However, still no particulars are known," the SSP said."It has come to the notice of the University that certain anti-social elements are spreading completely false, baseless and fabricated rumours through social media and other channels, thereby creating unnecessary confusion among students and attempting to disturb the peaceful academic environment of the University," said University registrar Dr Monica Gulati in a statement issued on Sunday morning."The manner in which such false and misleading information is being systematically circulated appears to be a deliberate and concerted attempt to malign the reputation of the University and tarnish its image. The University categorically clarifies that there is no truth in the rumours presently being circulated.""Students, parents and members of the public are requested not to believe, circulate or amplify such rumours. They should rely upon information communicated through official channels of the University only," Gulati said.
Article Summary: An unverified allegation that a girl student had been raped in a hostel triggered a protest at Lovely Professional University. Videos circulating on social media showed students damaging window panes, flower pots and even putting some objects on fire. Police officials said there was no complaint and that even during the protests, students could not provide any details about the alleged victim.

Article Title: Punjab man kills wife, daughter after domestic dispute
Article Text:
(Representative image) A man allegedly murdered his wife and their daughter in Amritsar after a domestic dispute





BATALA: A man is on the run after allegedly murdering his wife and minor daughter following a domestic dispute at their rented house in Amritsar late Friday night.Police said deep cuts were found on the necks of both victims, while the woman, 40-year-old Babli, had head injuries as well.The horror came to light on Saturday morning when the woman’s brother, after failing to get any response from her, went over to check and found the bodies of 40-year-old Babli and his 12-year-old niece lying near the staircase.Amritsar SSP Mehtab Singh said preliminary investigation indicated that a domestic dispute could have triggered the double murder, and that the woman’s husband, Jaswinder Masi, was involved.According to police and family members, the family lived in a rented house in Friends Colony. The woman’s brother Vijay alleged that Jaswinder was addicted to drugs and frequently assaulted his sister. He also demanded money from her to buy drugs, the family claimed.Babli worked as a domestic help to support the family and meet her daughter’s educational and household expenses. The family alleged that frequent quarrels took place after Babli and her daughter objected to Jaswinder’s drug use.Relatives alleged that Jaswinder had a heated argument with his daughter on Friday, and she told her maternal relatives about it. This may have triggered the grisly murders, say police. Forensic experts have gathered evidence from the crime scene and police teams are looking for Jaswinder. Investigators are checking CCTV footage to track the suspect’s movements.
Article Summary: A man is on the run after allegedly murdering his wife and minor daughter. Police said deep cuts were found on the necks of both victims, while the woman, 40-year-old Babli, had head injuries as well. The family alleged that frequent quarrels took place after Babli and her daughter objected to Jaswinder’s drug use.

Article Title: Russia backs India's claim to UNSC seat, firmly shuts door on Germany & Japan
Article Text:
Russian foreign minister Sergei Lavrov addresses the 81st United Nations General Assembly (Photo: Reuters).

Russia on Saturday backed a permanent seat for India and Brazil on the United Nations Security Council, while strongly opposing the same for Western countries.During his speech at the General Assembly, Russian foreign minister Sergei Lavrov said no additional seats at the UNSC should be given to Western countries, especially to Germany and the US ally, Japan.Russia has been one of the most consistent supporters of India’s bid for a permanent seat on the UN Security Council . Moscow has repeatedly backed India’s candidature as part of a broader push to make the Council more representative of Asia, Africa and Latin America.Lavrov has previously argued that the current composition no longer reflects today’s global balance and explicitly endorsed India, alongside Brazil, for permanent membership.This support was reiterated in the 2026 BRICS New Delhi Declaration, with China and Russia backing India and Brazil for a greater role in the UN, including the Security Council.Lavrov accused the West of continuously pumping weapons into Ukraine while helping target drones and missiles at Russia's civilians and civilian infrastructure.He also mentioned that Europe raised an anti-Moscow regime in Kyivv, in order to control the Russian influence."To pursue a utopian goal of containing Russia, the West dismantled the European security system and cultivated a Russophobic regime in Kyiv," he said, while warning the Western nations of "consequences".He further accused Europe of doing everything to block a peaceful settlement with Ukraine and disrupt negotiation prospects favoured by many, including the Trump administration.Lavrov claimed several EU leaders of being infected with racial superiority, encouraging the rise of what he called Ukrainian Nazism.The Russian foreign minister said the UN’s core principles were being put at risk, with the West overlooking the spread of Nazism in Ukraine.
Article Summary: Russia has been one of the most consistent supporters of India's bid for a permanent seat on the UN Security Council. Moscow has repeatedly backed India’s candidature as part of a broader push to make the Council more representative of Asia, Africa and Latin America.

Article Title: Winds, floods, 20-foot waves: What’s behind the nor’easter battering the US East Coast
Article Text:
Nor'easter pounding the Massachusetts coast with huge waves. (Source: X)

What is a nor’easter?

What is triggering this nor’easter?

What happens next?

America’s east coast is under a torrential attack as a powerful nor’easter is hammering the US East Coast, bringing heavy rain, strong winds, dangerous surf and coastal flooding from the Mid-Atlantic to New England.More than 100,000 homes and businesses lost power at one point as the storm knocked down trees, branches and power lines across the region. More than 88,000 customers remained without electricity in New Jersey, Connecticut, New York and Pennsylvania as of Saturday afternoon.The storm has also disrupted travel, with around 425 flights cancelled and more than 1,300 delayed across US airports, according to FlightAware.The National Weather Service warned that the storm could continue bringing coastal flooding, rip currents, strong wind gusts and heavy rain through Monday. The biggest threat was expected along coastal and bayside communities, where exceptionally high tides could send water onto roads and into homes and businesses.In New Jersey and New York, flooded streets became so deep that some residents took to kayaks. Along the coast, powerful waves battered beaches, eroded dunes and damaged property.In Surf City, New Jersey, water is rising inside houses as people’s belongings also get displaced by the strong forces of wind and rain.In Ocean City, Maryland, heavy surf eroded beaches and washed away dune fencing. In Norfolk, Virginia, flooding left vehicles struggling through waterlogged roads.The disruption extended well beyond homes and roads. Flights were cancelled, sporting events were rescheduled and concerts and festivals were called off as the storm moved slowly along the coast.A nor’easter is a powerful storm that develops along or near the US East Coast, typically moving northeastward while drawing energy from the contrast between cold air to the north and warmer, moist air to the south and over the Atlantic.The storms get their name from the northeasterly winds that can batter the coast as the system strengthens.They can bring a dangerous combination of heavy rain, powerful winds, coastal flooding and huge waves. Heavy rainfall can overwhelm drainage systems and worsen inland flooding, while strong gusts can bring down trees, damage buildings and snap power lines. High tides, combined with storm-driven water, can push seawater onto roads and into coastal communities. Meanwhile, prolonged strong winds can whip up dangerous surf and accelerate beach and dune erosion.This storm is particularly threatening because it is slow-moving. That means coastal areas can remain exposed to strong winds, waves and high water for a prolonged period rather than getting a quick hit and recovery.The immediate ingredients are the storm’s atmospheric setup, strong winds, moisture and the temperature contrasts that help nor’easters intensify.But there is a bigger climate pattern in the background: El Niño.El Niño is a natural cycle in the tropical Pacific in which unusually warm ocean temperatures alter atmospheric circulation far beyond the Pacific.This year’s El Niño is particularly strong. Its effects are being felt across the US, although scientists stress that it does not directly cause every individual storm.For the Northeast, El Niño can shift the Pacific jet stream southward. That atmospheric pattern can help provide energy and moisture for storms forming off the southeastern US before they move north along the East Coast.Nor’easters also appear to occur more frequently during El Niño years, according to a New York Times report.For the East Coast, the immediate concern remains water and wind.The highest tides were expected north of Atlantic City from Saturday night into Sunday, raising the risk of widespread flooding in coastal and bayside communities.Tens of millions of people remained in the storm’s path, while emergency agencies prepared for further outages and flooding.And while nor’easters are a familiar part of the Northeast’s colder months, forecasters said this storm arrived somewhat earlier than usual for a system of this strength.El Niño is also expected to influence other weather patterns through the coming months, researchers are currently keeping an eye on what they should expect next.
Article Summary: More than 100,000 homes and businesses lost power at one point. More than 88,000 customers remained without electricity in New Jersey, Connecticut, New York and Pennsylvania as of Saturday afternoon. The storm has also disrupted travel, with around 425 flights cancelled and more than 1,300 delayed across US airports.

Article Title: 'Ma, they punched me in chest': Student's last call before death at Guwahati homestay; accused claims she 'hanged' herself
Article Text:
Both Nimisha and Ashiq were staying in the homestay together in Dharapur during the time of the incident.

'Will stay at hostel with friends'

'She did not mention homestay'

Police examine Ashiq's account

Homestay verification under scanner

Residents demand investigation

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think is the most concerning aspect of this case? Lack of proper verification by the homestay Possible involvement of love jihad Delayed police response 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





GUWAHATI: “Ma, they have beaten me. They punched me in the chest and assaulted me. I am injured," these were the words 22-year-old Gauhati University student Nimisha Thakuria allegedly told her mother over the phone around 2 am on Saturday, according to her father Deep Thakuria.The family could not reach her after the call and later learnt that she had been found in a critical condition at a homestay on the outskirts of Guwahati.Nimisha was taken to Garal Primary Health Centre and later referred to Gauhati Medical College and Hospital, where doctors declared her dead on arrival.Police have detained her alleged companion, 26-year-old Ashiq Ali, and are investigating the circumstances surrounding her death.Deep Thakuria said Nimisha left home around 5 pm on Friday and told her mother she might spend the night at Gauhati University hostel with friends.“She had told her mother that she would stay at Gauhati University hostel with her friends,” he said.Around 10 pm, Nimisha again told her mother that she would spend the night there.But around 2 am, she called her mother unexpectedly. “After that, we could no longer reach her.We kept calling her repeatedly, but there was no response,” Thakuria added further.The family eventually contacted Azara police station, where an officer tried to trace Nimisha's phone location.The father also told TOI, that he and his family went to Azara police station and informed the second officer-in-charge about the situation.Around half an hour later, police told the family that a girl had been found at Garal Primary Health Centre and asked them to verify whether she was Nimisha.He said police told them that if the woman was Nimisha, she would be taken immediately to Gauhati Medical College and Hospital.Thakuria said Nimisha had not told the family that she planned to stay at a homestay with Ashiq Ali.Instead, he said, she had told them she would be staying at the university hostel with friends. “She took Rs 2,000 just two days back, saying she would go out to eat with her friends and stay overnight at a friend's hostel,” he said.Police said Nimisha and Ashiq had been staying at a homestay in the Dharapur-Garal area. They are examining their movements and the events leading up to Nimisha being found unconscious.Ashiq told police that Nimisha had hanged herself and died by suicide.Deputy commissioner of police (west) Balin Deuri said investigators would establish whether that account was true.“Whether it is true or a lie, would come out during the investigation,” Deuri said.The body has been sent for post-mortem examination, and police are awaiting the report. CID and forensic teams have also examined the homestay room and collected evidence.Police said Nimisha and Ashiq had visited the homestay five times this month and were allowed to stay without proper verification.The homestay had also not collected mandatory identification documents from the two, police said. Its owner has been questioned and action will be initiated under the law.A staff member, Bipul Bailung, said Nimisha and Ashiq were staying in room number 10 and had ordered food around 9.30 pm.He claimed staff later heard shouts for help and crying in a male voice around 2.30-3 am.“Three of us went to their room and found the girl lying on the floor, with the boy holding her in his hands and crying,” Bailung said.After news of Nimisha's death spread, local residents blocked a road leading towards the nearby airport and staged a protest demanding a thorough investigation.Some protesters alleged that the incident was linked to what they described as “love jihad”.“We demand a proper investigation and justice so that no one involved in the incident is allowed to escape accountability. Those responsible should be identified and brought to justice,” a protester said.Nimisha's last rites were performed on Saturday evening after her body was handed over to her family following the post-mortem.
Article Summary: Gauhati University student Nimisha Thakuria, 22, was found dead at a homestay in Guwahati. Her alleged companion, 26-year-old Ashiq Ali, has been detained. Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding her death.

Article Title: Mojtaba Khamenei ‘pulled from rubble’ after US-Israeli strikes hit Tehran hospital: Report
Article Text:
Iran’s Mojtaba Khamenei ‘pulled from rubble’ after hospital hit by US-Israeli strikes

Iran’s supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei was reportedly “pulled from the rubble” of a Tehran hospital after US and Israeli strikes hit the medical centre where he had been taken following earlier attacks, the New York Post reported.Mohsen Heydari, a member of Iran’s Assembly of Experts, made the revelation in an interview with Qatari television network Al Araby on Thursday.“Even after he had been wounded and taken to the hospital, three hospitals in Tehran were bombed,” Heydari said. Mojtaba Khamenei was in the third hospital and was pulled from the rubble,” he said.Speculation has continued over Mojtaba Khamenei’s condition following the earlier strikes. US intelligence reports had reportedly indicated that he was badly disfigured in the attacks.According to the report, Heydari also spoke about the process through which Mojtaba Khamenei was selected as Iran’s new supreme leader on March 8. He said Mojtaba apparently did not know he had been chosen until the announcement was broadcast on Iranian state television.The Assembly of Experts, which is responsible for selecting Iran’s supreme leader, was itself reportedly targeted in the strikes.The New York Post reported that its Qom Secretariat was bombed, killing eight people and destroying reports and recommendations related to the selection of a new supreme leader.Heydari said members of the Assembly subsequently recorded their votes on paper before being summoned to a secret room for the selection process. He recalled being the first member to propose Mojtaba Khamenei’s name.“Given the enemy’s position, we will choose and elect no one as leader and supreme guide of the Islamic Republic except Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei,” Heydari said.“We obtained information that Mojtaba Khamenei was healthy and able to lead, and we determined that he met the requirements of religious qualification, justice and competence to manage the country,” he said.Heydari also described Mojtaba Khamenei as a “man of the shadows”, saying he had not held any political position within the Iranian state before becoming supreme leader, although he had reportedly served as an adviser to his father.
Article Summary: Iran’s supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei was reportedly ‘pulled from the rubble’ of a Tehran hospital. US and Israeli strikes hit the medical centre where he had been taken following earlier attacks. US intelligence reports had reportedly indicated that he was badly disfigured in the attacks.
